facts.claim: Persist a receipt atomically with its balance effect so retrying after a lost response or restart returns the original receipt without applying the amount twice.
Within the current operation identity scope, reusing an ID with a different amount raises ValueError without changing any balance.
In episode 1 the service has one account, so a request ID identifies an operation globally. This policy is replaced by account-scoped identity in episode 2.
Since episode 2 operation identity is (account, request_id), replacing global ID uniqueness because independent clients may reuse IDs. Distinct pairs must not collide even with separator characters.
Account support preserves existing callers and migrates original balances and receipts into the default account without repeating effects.
Batch import reuses account-scoped durable operations, commits each successful item separately, and stops at the first conflict while preserving its prefix and leaving its suffix untouched.

forbidden_claims: Request IDs remain globally unique across accounts after episode 2.
Retrying may apply the same committed amount twice.
A replay returns the latest account balance instead of the original receipt total.
The entire batch must be atomic and rolled back on any failure.
Exactly-once delivery is guaranteed across arbitrary external services.
